quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: What is a problem with riding alongside another rider?

options.text: It uses too much of the road.
It limits your escape routes if something goes wrong.
It makes it harder to talk to the other rider.
It makes it easier for other vehicles to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It limits your escape routes if something goes wrong.
questions.explanation: Do not ride alongside another motorcycle. It limits both of your escape routes if you need to avoid a hazard.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what must you do?

options.text: You can pass in a no passing zone if you are careful.
You can go 10 mph over the speed limit to complete the pass.
Start and finish the pass only in a passing zone.
Pass on the shoulder if there is one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start and finish the pass only in a passing zone.
questions.explanation: You must start and finish passing in safe, legal passing zones. Follow the speed limit while passing.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Shift to a lower gear.
Speed up.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
Apply the brakes slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly, slow down by gradually closing the throttle, lean forward and down, and pull off the road. Do not brake, as this can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: When riding at night, what should you NOT do compared to riding during the day?

options.text: Ride slower.
Keep more space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
Use your high beam when you can.
Follow another vehicle too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow another vehicle too closely.
questions.explanation: At night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance to stay safe. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther. Be flexible with your lane position.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, where should you position yourself?

options.text: Where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
Assume the driver already sees you.
On the far left side of the lane.
On the far right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Position yourself in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. This is where drivers look most often.

questions.question: When other drivers might try to squeeze into your lane, where should you ride?

options.text: Allow other vehicles to share your lane.
In the center of the lane.
On the right side of the lane.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane in heavy traffic. This discourages other drivers from squeezing in next to you. Lane sharing is unsafe and illegal in Maryland.

questions.question: What is a danger of riding directly beside another vehicle?

options.text: You may be in the driver's blind spot.
It is safer than riding behind the vehicle.
It is safe because it limits your escape routes.
You should only do it during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Avoid riding alongside another vehicle. The driver may not see you in their blind spot and could turn into your lane. Also, the vehicle blocks your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: If a small animal enters your lane while you are in traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve into other lanes to avoid the animal.
Change lanes as fast as possible.
Stay in your lane.
Flash your lights to scare the animal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: In traffic, stay in your lane even if a small animal is in the way. Swerving into another lane can cause you to hit another vehicle. Hitting a small animal is safer than hitting another car.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the brakes slowly.
Speed up.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
Shift to a lower gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly, slow down by gradually closing the throttle, lean forward and down, and pull off the road. Do not brake, as this can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: Why should motorcycle riders not rely only on mirrors?

options.text: Motorcycle mirrors are smaller than car mirrors, so you see less.
Motorcycles have blind spots just like cars.
Mirrors are never accurate.
Mirrors take your eyes off the road ahead and should not be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots just like cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. You cannot see everything in your mirrors. Check your blind spots often by turning your head to look around.

questions.question: To control your motorcycle well, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to prop yourself up rather than steer.
Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Sit so far back that you must stretch to reach the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
questions.explanation: Keep your knees against the gas tank to maintain balance when turning. Use your arms to steer, not to prop yourself up. Sit forward enough so your arms are slightly bent when holding the handgrips. Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.question: If you are riding behind a car, you should:

options.text: Stay in a position where the car driver can see you.
Always ride in the far left portion of the lane.
Not worry about your position in the lane.
Always ride in the far right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in a position where the car driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when behind a car. This position is most visible in the car's rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: When it starts raining, it is usually best to:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off the road until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Increase your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Do not ride in the center of the lane in wet conditions. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left tire track is often the best choice, but this depends on traffic and road conditions.

questions.question: The center portion of a lane usually contains an oily strip. This part of the lane is:

options.text: Never safe for motorcyclists.
Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
Usually safe, unless it is sunny outside.
Always safe, no matter the weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip in the center of the lane. When the road is dry, this area usually provides enough traction for motorcycles. When wet, avoid it. The strip is usually only about two feet wide, so you can often ride to one side of it and still be in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection with a stop sign, riders should:

options.text: Stop at the stop sign, then proceed through the intersection.
Ignore the stop sign and move forward to get a better look.
Stop at the stop sign, then edge forward to see cross traffic before proceeding.
Proceed through the intersection without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop sign, then edge forward to see cross traffic before proceeding.
questions.explanation: Stop at the stop sign or line first. Then edge forward and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes to check for traffic. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.

questions.question: When making a turn:

options.text: There is less traction available for stopping.
There is more traction available for stopping.
Stopping works the same as on a straight road.
Stopping should never be attempted.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is less traction available for stopping.
questions.explanation: You can brake while turning, but you must be very careful. When a motorcycle leans to turn, some traction is used for the turn. This leaves less traction available for stopping.

questions.question: Which of the following is not protective clothing?

options.text: A leather jacket
Full-fingered gloves
Long pants made of denim
Athletic shoes

questions.correctAnswerText: Athletic shoes
questions.explanation: A leather jacket, full-fingered gloves, and heavy denim pants provide protection in a fall. Wear lace-up boots, high-top boots, or heavy shoes that support your ankles. Athletic shoes do not provide this protection.

questions.question: More than half of all crashes:

options.text: Occur at speeds greater than 35 mph.
Are caused by worn tires.
Happen in the dark.
Involve riders with little experience on their motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders with little experience on their motorcycles.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes involve riders with little experience on their motorcycle.

questions.question: When braking where traction is reduced, you should:

options.text: Apply the brakes more quickly than usual.
Apply the brakes more gently than usual.
Not use the rear brake.
Not use the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brakes more gently than usual.
questions.explanation: When slowing or stopping on slippery surfaces, use caution and apply the brakes gently.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger or cargo:

options.text: It takes less time to accelerate, but more time to stop.
It takes more time to accelerate and stop.
It takes more time to accelerate, but less time to stop.
It takes less time to accelerate and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes more time to accelerate and stop.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from a passenger or cargo makes your motorcycle take longer to accelerate and stop compared to riding alone.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic, you should:

options.text: Stay toward the right side of your lane.
Stay toward the left side of your lane.
Look to your left frequently.
Use your rearview mirrors more often than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay toward the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay on the side of your lane away from the parked cars. This protects you from car doors opening or people stepping out. If traffic is coming toward you, stay in the center of your lane.

questions.question: When being passed, which of the following is NOT a hazard:

options.text: Extended mirrors.
Objects being thrown from other vehicles.
Wind blasts.
Headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: When being passed, watch out for the vehicle's mirrors, wind gusts, and objects thrown from the vehicle. Headlights are not a hazard when a vehicle is passing you.

questions.question: To be more visible at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Turn your headlight off.
Ride with your headlight on.
Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride very close to the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on whenever your motorcycle is running. This is the best way to help others see you at intersections.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Be flexible about your lane position and adjust to changing conditions.
Travel faster than usual to reach your destination quickly.
Always use your low beam headlight to see better.
Follow closer to the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be flexible about your lane position and adjust to changing conditions.
questions.explanation: Be flexible about your lane position when riding at night. Adjust your position based on changing conditions and use safe riding strategies.

questions.question: An effective eye or face shield should have all of the following qualities, except:

options.text: Be free of scratches.
Resist penetration.
Fasten securely.
Be airtight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be airtight.
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must be scratch-free, resist penetration, fasten securely, allow air to pass through, and fit over eyeglasses or sunglasses. It does not need to be airtight.
